text:
1 hours ago Kingston officials voice support for Lisa Baker
We are writing to express our strong support for Lisa Baker in her campaign for re-election as State Senator in our 20th District. Lisa has a long-standing history and proven record for thoughtful leadership, integrity, and practical vision in our community of Kingston and Northeastern Pennsylvania. She is a leader who has exemplified the meaning of serving the public good.
What distinguishes Lisa is not only her experience, but her ability to listen, engage, and act with purpose. Throughout her career, she has demonstrated a clear understanding of the challenges facing our communities-whether it be economic growth, education, healthcare, public safety, or infrastructure-and has consistently worked toward solutions that are both realistic and forward-thinking.
We are all longstanding elected and appointed officials of the Municipality of Kingston.
Lisa has always gone out of her way to deliver grants and resources to Kingston that have changed the face of the community and saved millions of dollars that would otherwise be borrowed or taken from general funds. Some of the notable projects that she supported include improvements to the Kingston Community Pool, new lighting systems for our Little League fields at Keiper Park, new soccer fields and playground equipment at Church Street Park, and significant funds for remodeling our police department and municipal building.
Additionally, Lisa brings a level of senior leadership, professionalism, and respect to public discourse that is often lacking. She has demonstrated civility and sought common ground where possible, without compromising on core values. This kind of leadership helps unify rather than divide and fosters a healthier political climate for everyone.
We wholeheartedly believe that Lisa Baker is the clear choice for State Senator in our 20th District. We encourage others to learn more about her platform and not to be buffaloed by the smear campaign that is being brought against her by self-interest PAC money.
Thank you for your time and consideration.
Signed by Kingston Pa. officials,
Nancy Cooper, Robert Jacobs, Paul Keating, Allan Littzi, and Robert Thompson
Something needs to be done to stop gun violence in schools
Since the 1999 Columbine school shootings, 390,000 students have experienced gun violence in their schools across the country. Many suffer from PTSD; they have anxiety about going to school, with 417 school shootings since Columbine. 440 students and educators have been killed in K-12 grades, with 1,243 injured in the US. In 2026 alone, 99 school gunfire incidents resulted in 106 deaths and 374 injuries.
Innocent children who will never grow up, go to college, get married, or become leaders in their communities, teachers, doctors, lawyers, and yes, politicians holding office that could have prevented this by passing common sense gun safety laws.
Gun violence is the number one killer of children under the age of 19 in the US, not cancer, not childhood diseases, not car accidents.
The failure by Congress to pass gun safety laws addressing school gun violence over the last 25 years has had lasting effects for millions of children going to school worried they may not make it home. Saying goodbye to their families has become a ritual, knowing it may be the last time they will see them.
As if they were going off to war. Maybe they are in a way. Assault military-style rifles were only meant for wartime, for soldiers to kill as many targets as possible in minutes, not in the hands of civilians with revenge on their minds or mental health crises.
The children’s empty rooms, untouched, was a documentary short film that won the Academy Award this year. It showed the contents of a child’s room intact, with families left to mourn and decide what to do with childhood memories: toys, games, trophies, cards, pictures, posters, stuffed animals and their dreams for the future.
No child wants to die because lawmakers refuse to protect them with gun safety measures. Children have no voice or vote on the matter. Gun manufacturers made one billion dollars in the past 10 years, selling AR15 style rifles to civilians. Smith and Wesson and others have come under scrutiny from gun safety advocates for their questionable marketing practices, with calls for regulation. Marketing assault rifles to young men ” who are attracted to violence and military fantasies” has matched the profiles of school shooters across the country. Ads portray them as if their masculinity required an “AR15 strapped across their chest.”
Common sense gun safety laws are needed: extended background checks, secure firearms storage laws, banning assault weapons with large capacity magazines, red flag laws, mental health practitioners in schools, training teachers/students to “KNOW THE SIGNS” of anyone at risk to themselves or others, no tolerance policy for bullying.
Most shooters have a school connection; many shootings are targeted with warning signs. Half of the school shootings occur when a child/teen accesses a firearm found in the home. Nearly 4.6 million children live in homes with at least one loaded and unlocked gun.
Our children deserve better from lawmakers with the power to save lives with common-sense gun laws.
Karen Prohonic
Swoyersville, PA
